questions.text:
Consider the productions [latex]A\rightarrow PQ[/latex] and [latex]A\rightarrow XY[/latex]. Each of the five non-terminals A,P,Q,X, and Y has two attributes: s is a synthesized attribute, and i is an inherited attribute. Consider the following rules.

Rule 1: P.i=A.i+2, Q.i=P.i+A.i, and A.s=P.s+Q.s
Rule 2: X.i=A.i+Y.s and Y.i=X.s+A.i

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
L-attributed: an inherited attribute may depend only on the parent's inherited attributes and on attributes of siblings to its left.

- Rule 1: P.i uses A.i; Q.i uses P.i (left sibling) and A.i [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] L-attributed.
- Rule 2: X.i uses Y.s, and Y is to the right of X [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not L-attributed.

Answer: Only Rule 1 is L-attributed

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both Rule 1 and Rule 2 are L-attributed.
Neither Rule 1 nor Rule 2 is L-attributed.

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar.

[latex]S\rightarrow aSB|d[/latex]
[latex]B\rightarrow b[/latex]

The number of reduction steps taken by a bottom-up parser while accepting the string [latex]aaadbbb[/latex] is___________.
questions.solution:
Reductions while parsing aaadbbb bottom-up:
1. d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S
2. b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B, 3. aSB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S
4. b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B, 5. aSB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S
6. b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B, 7. aSB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S

Answer: 7

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

I. Symbol table is accessed only during lexical analysis and syntax analysis.
II. Compilers for programming languages that support recursion necessarily need heap storage for memory allocation in the run-time environment.
III. Errors violating the condition 'any variable must be declared before its use' are detected during syntax analysis.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: the symbol table is used in later phases too (semantic analysis, code generation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: recursion needs a stack of activation records, not a heap [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: "declare before use" is a context-sensitive check done in semantic analysis [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: None of I, II and III

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: None of I, II and III

questions.text:
Consider the augmented grammar given below:
[latex]S'\rightarrow S[/latex]
[latex]S \rightarrow \lt L \gt |id[/latex]
[latex]L \rightarrow L,S|S[/latex]

Let [latex]I_0=CLOSURE(\{[S'\rightarrow \cdot S]\}) [/latex]. The number of items in the set [latex]GOTO(I_0,\lt)[/latex] is __________.
questions.solution:
In [latex]I_0[/latex], the item [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot\lt L\gt[/latex] moves on [latex]\lt[/latex] to [latex]S\rightarrow\lt\cdot L\gt[/latex]. Closure (dot before L, then before S):
1. [latex]S\rightarrow\lt\cdot L\gt[/latex]
2. [latex]L\rightarrow\cdot L,S[/latex]
3. [latex]L\rightarrow\cdot S[/latex]
4. [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot\lt L\gt[/latex]
5. [latex]S\rightarrow\cdot id[/latex]

Answer: 5

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar and the semantic actions to support the inherited type declaration attributes. Let [latex]X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,X_5 \; and \; X_6[/latex] be the placeholders for the non-terminals D, T, L or [latex]L_1[/latex] in the following table:

Which one of the following are the appropriate choices for [latex]X_1,X_2,X_3 \; and \; X_4[/latex]?
questions.solution:
The type flows from T to the list L (inherited attribute):
- D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T L: the list gets T's type [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L.type=T.type[/latex], so [latex]X_1=L,\ X_2=T[/latex].
- L [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L_1[/latex], id: pass the type down to [latex]L_1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L_1.type=L.type[/latex], so [latex]X_3=L_1,\ X_4=L[/latex] (and id gets L.type).

Answer: [latex]X_1=L,X_2=T,X_3=L_1,X_4=L[/latex]
